label: LC/UPC connector pair
notes: 0.25 dB is a typical loss for a mated LC/UPC pair and 0.50 dB is the ceiling it is held to, which is IEC 61753-1 attenuation grade C for random mating (0.25 dB mean, 0.50 dB max); grade B is 0.12 dB mean and 0.25 dB max. Typical and grade figures, not one vendor's test report. The row is here because polish is a physical contact, not a tolerance: all eleven transceivers in this catalogue are UPC - the Cisco SFP-10G-ZR row says so in as many words, 'dual LC/PC; APC patch cords are not supported' - while the only LC connector row was LC/APC, so an active link had to be budgeted with a mating that cannot plug into its own optic. The engine charges lossDb per mating and does not compare polish against the optic, so there is no refusal to lean on: ask for this row (connectorModel, or connectors: { model: 'lc-upc', count: n }) and get a UPC figure. Reachability is worth stating plainly - engine/link.js charges the default sc-apc pair at both ends of an active link and takes no connector model, so this row is selectable through budget.pointToPoint and the design API today, and wiring it into link design is an engine change rather than a catalogue one. Replace with the loss measured on the patch cords you buy.
